name: Silverstein
label: Victory
lede: Shane Told formed Silverstein in Burlington, Ontario in 2000 as a side project, learned to scream because his guitarist asked, and then watched four Victory records get sung back to the band word for word.

eras.title: A punk kid learns to scream
eras.text: Silverstein started in 2000 as a side project for Shane Told, then 19 and still in the punk band Jerk Circus. Guitarist Josh Bradford wanted a screamer, so Told taught himself, and by October 2002 Victory Records had signed them.

years.h: Shane Told's side project borrows its name from Shel Silverstein
years.p: Told is 19 and still in the punk band Jerk Circus when he starts it in February 2000. The name comes from the children's author the members grew up reading.
years.xp: Told was in his first year at the University of Guelph, studying music, genetics and molecular biology. Jerk Circus rehearsed in his parents' basement, put out Never Mind the Suburbs in 2001 and the EP Everything Is a Travesty with You, and split in 2002.

years.h: Six months in, the band self-releases Summer's Stellar Gaze
years.p: The first EP comes out in August 2000 with no label behind it.

years.h: A message-board post brings in bassist Billy Hamilton
years.p: Hamilton reads on The 905 Board that the band needs a bass player, and joins in December 2000.

years.h: Neil Boshart takes over lead guitar from Richard McWalter
years.p: McWalter, the original guitarist, moves to Victoria, British Columbia to study engineering.
years.xp: The five-piece that results, Told, Boshart, Bradford, Hamilton and Paul Koehler on drums, stays together for more than a decade.

years.h: Josh Bradford wants a screamer, so Shane Told teaches himself
years.p: Told's first try at harsh vocals is a contest at Warped Tour. The first record that shows it is the 2002 EP When the Shadows Beam.
years.xp: Told practiced in remote spots so he wouldn't disturb his housemates. According to Wikipedia, the noise drew police attention on several occasions, and none of those visits went further.

years.h: Victory Records takes on a band not yet three years old
years.p: The Chicago label signs Silverstein in October 2002, with Boshart, Bradford, Hamilton, Koehler and Told in place.

eras.title: School out, debut in
eras.text: Told quit the University of Guelph a month before the first album came out. It was made in five weeks in southern Ontario and sold far past anyone's expectations.

years.h: Shane Told quits Guelph a month before the debut
years.p: He walks away from music, genetics and molecular biology in April 2003. Two songs from the album, Smashed Into Pieces and Giving Up, go online April 3 and 5.

years.src: Wikipedia: When Broken Is Easily Fixed · Wikipedia: Silverstein
years.h: When Broken Is Easily Fixed comes out of two studios in two months
years.p: Justin Koop recorded and mixed it at Mount Fairview and Unity Gain in January and February 2003. It had sold 179,000 copies by June 2007.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's band page puts the sales at over 200,000. Alternative Press called it one of the most deeply personal and creative albums of 2003.

On May 20, 2013, ten years to the day, the band released a re-recorded Smashed Into Pieces.

years.h: Victory reissues the debut with a live DVD attached
years.p: Bonus tracks come with it, plus concert footage and band interviews on the DVD.

eras.title: A studio tantrum, then the Top 40
eras.text: Discovering the Waterfront put Silverstein in the Billboard Top 40 and on Warped Tour. Shane Told wrecked studio gear while making it, and Victory Records paid the bill.

yt: Smile in Your Sleep, official video
years.h: Discovering the Waterfront enters the Billboard 200 at No. 34
years.p: Cameron Webb produced it at Capitol Studios in Hollywood, and 26,229 copies sold in week one. It passed 100,000 in the US by the end of 2005.
years.xp:
Sales reached 232,000 by June 2007, and the band later said 400,000. Music Canada certified it Gold on September 5, 2024.

A September 2006 reissue added a DVD and the bonus track Rodeo Clown. Smile in Your Sleep went to radio July 19, 2005, a month before the album.

years.h: Shane Told wrecks studio gear over My Heroine
years.p: Producer Cameron Webb and the band were skeptical of the song, and Told, who wanted it kept, started breaking things. Victory Records paid for the damage.
years.xp:
Told wanted a different track, Always and Never, cut, because he didn't know what to do vocally on it. Both stayed, and the album ended up at 11 songs.

My Heroine got a video along with Smile in Your Sleep and the title track. Loudwire later named Smile in Your Sleep and My Heroine classic anthems of the 2000s screamo movement.

years.h: Two summers on Warped Tour, plus two package tours
years.p: Silverstein spends 2005 and 2006 on the Vans Warped Tour, the Never Sleep Again Tour and Taste of Chaos.
years.xp: The 2005 Warped Tour run went from mid-June to mid-August. Never Sleep Again followed in late 2005, two months across the US with Hawthorne Heights, Bayside, Spitalfield and Aiden.

years.h: [[Bedouin Soundclash|e0036453-ce34-4095-af40-8c70ee07cef1]] beats Silverstein for the 2006 Juno
years.p: The category is New Group of the Year, and Silverstein is up for it three years after its debut.

years.h: An American Idol hopeful brings inhale screams to the audition
years.p: Ryan Heart performs Smashed Into Pieces for the judges. Alternative Press reported they weren't impressed.

years.cap: Silverstein live in Chemnitz, Germany, June 2007
years.h: Arrivals & Departures goes to No. 1 on the indie chart
years.p: Mark Trombino produced it in March 2007. It opened at No. 25 on the Billboard 200 with about 27,000 sold in the first week.
years.xp:
The band went for a stripped-down sound. Told said in 2018 that "it wasn't a super slick record like Discovering The Waterfront", with fewer guitar tracks, rawer drums and little backing vocal. Some fans, expecting the old post-hardcore, were disappointed.

Reviews were generally positive. Bradford said Trombino's production suited what the band wanted. A remixed and remastered 26-track edition came out December 2, 2022.
play: If You Could See into My Soul

eras.title: A mutiny on record, a new label
eras.text: Silverstein's fourth album was a four-chapter concept record about a mutiny, and it closed out the Victory contract. By November 2010 the band was on Hopeless.

years.cap: Neil Boshart on stage in Corpus Christi, Texas, April 10, 2009
years.src: Wikipedia: A Shipwreck in the Sand · Wikipedia: Silverstein
years.h: A crew mutinies in four chapters on A Shipwreck in the Sand
years.p: No land appears, so the crew turns on its captain, which Shane Told called a metaphor for betrayal. It opened at No. 33 on the Billboard 200, one place above Discovering the Waterfront.
years.xp:
The 14 tracks split into four chapters: It Burns Within Us All, Liars, Cheaters and Thieves, Fight Fire with Fire, and Death and Taxes. The album's site promised "Betrayal. Arson. Infidelity. True Love."

Liam Cormier of [[Cancer Bats|00b952be-6c97-4880-84f9-06de584b491b]] guests on Vices and Scott Wade of [[Comeback Kid|6d152109-c447-446d-9a06-3621c920bebd]] on Born Dead, which takes on American health care; Lights also guests. Vices got a video March 17, directed by Robby Starbuck.

Cameron Webb came back to produce at Metalworks in Mississauga because the band was unhappy with how Arrivals & Departures sounded. It was the last of the four Victory albums.

years.h: Decade puts ten years on DVD, live at the El Mocambo
years.p: It comes out June 8, 2010, as a DVD and CD, ten years after the band formed in Burlington.

years.cap: Shane Told rises above the crowd in Milwaukee
years.h: Silverstein walks out of its Victory contract
years.p: The band leaves Victory in October 2010 and signs with Hopeless Records on November 15, with Universal Music handling Canada.
years.xp:
Told described the next music that year as "a cross between Discovering the Waterfront and A Shipwreck in the Sand". The band spent late 2010 on the Scream It Like You Mean It Tour with Emery, We Came As Romans and Dance Gavin Dance, among others.

The label path from here: Hopeless and Universal Canada until 2014, Rise Records until 2019, then UNFD.

eras.title: The band that wouldn't leave
eras.text: Silverstein never broke up. It lost a guitarist after 11 years, moved from Hopeless to Rise to UNFD, collected two more Juno nominations, and kept playing its Victory-era records to crowds who grew up on them.

years.h: Rescue is the fifth album and the first on Hopeless
years.p: It follows the December 2010 EP Transitions, the band's first release after Victory.

years.h: Short Songs keeps every track under a minute and a half
years.p: There are 22 of them, and half are covers of punk songs.

years.cap: Shane Told, Josh Bradford, Paul Koehler, Billy Hamilton and Paul Marc Rousseau
years.h: Neil Boshart leaves after 11 years, and Paul Marc Rousseau steps in
years.p: Rousseau, formerly of I Am Committing a Sin, takes his place in the lineup that Boshart had been part of since 2001.

years.cap: Shane Told on stage at the Two Days a Week festival
years.h: Ten years on, Discovering the Waterfront gets a world tour
years.p: The 2005 album goes out worldwide again in 2015, the same year the band is back on Warped Tour.
years.xp: The band also put out I Am Alive in Everything I Touch that year, on May 19, during the Rise Records stretch.

years.cap: Silverstein at the Impericon Festival, Oberhausen, April 21, 2018
years.h: When Broken Is Easily Fixed turns 15 and goes back on tour
years.p: Silverstein plays the 2003 debut on an anniversary tour that runs from 2018 into 2019.

years.h: A Beautiful Place to Drown becomes a Juno nominee
years.p: The first album since the band joined UNFD in 2019 is up for Rock Album of the Year at the 2021 Junos.
years.xp: Singles around it came with guests: Caleb Shomo of Beartooth on Burn It Down in June 2019, Aaron Gillespie of Underoath on Infinite in January 2020, and Princess Nokia on Madness in March 2020.

years.cap: Silverstein at Rock am Ring, Germany
years.h: Antibloom and Pink Moon arrive seven months apart
years.p: Antibloom comes out February 21, 2025 and Pink Moon September 19. The band tours the pair as 25 Years of Noise.
years.xp:
Antibloom is nominated for a 2026 Juno, in the Heavy Metal Album of the Year category. The band page counts 13 studio albums, seven EPs and over a million albums sold worldwide.

The 2026 touring includes a run with Story of the Year and Origami Angel.
